correctness.rationale: For every model state the susceptibility multipliers lie in \([0,1]\), so \(R_e\le\tau\); therefore \(\tau<1\) forces zero infections. Under zero infections the population vector shifts one class per season, reaching \(p_r=1\) after exactly \(r-1\) seasons, while the immunity recursion after that block depends only on drifts inside the block. This yields the stated common conditional law and global minorization. The total-variation contraction, existence and uniqueness of the stationary law, and the blockwise rate follow directly. The finite checker replays representative exact-rational updates but is not used as the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper proves stationary convergence only under a complete-drift atom and explicitly leaves removal of that assumption open for general finite immunity memory. The new proof uses a different, state-independent coalescence mechanism: an \(r-1\)-season block with transmissibility below one makes every outbreak zero, shifts all population mass to the nonimmune class, and leaves the immunity vector as a function only of within-block drifts. This gives a model-specific global minorization and explicit total-variation rate. Exact-title/identifier searches, equivalent regeneration/minorization searches, the current published-finding database, and the full motivating article did not reveal that statement. Standard Doeblin literature covers only the abstract implication once the minorization has been found.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies removal of the complete-drift atom as an unresolved proof issue for general \(r\). The finding resolves that issue under the natural and much weaker condition \(\mathbb P(\tau<1)>0\), and additionally provides an initialization-uniform quantitative burn-in bound for stationary simulations and predictions. The mechanism uses the model's finite immunity memory rather than a generic relabeling or parameter substitution.
